name: Wilhelm II
role: German Emperor and King of Prussia (1888-1918)
summary: Wilhelm II ruled as a monarch who claimed his crown by God's grace, distrusted parliament and the Social Democrats, and personally promoted the army, the navy and Weltpolitik. He backed worker-protection legislation while treating socialism as the enemy, and in exile voiced antisemitic and conspiratorial views. He also took a conservative line on art, religion, women's roles and education.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Memoirs: his worker-protection laws were a handicap on German industry and alienated industrial leaders, but he pressed on for the welfare of the whole nation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Prided himself on social insurance and worker protection laws and told workers he had improved their condition, in the memoirs and speeches of 1902 and 1906.

strong-leader.rationale: Memoirs say a monarch can and must influence the realm by personal participation and pick ministers independent of party; he is reported as saying only one person is master in the Empire.

empower-police-military.rationale: Asked the Reichstag for larger army and navy budgets (1893 army bill, naval programme) and wrote that the army and navy needed strength.

traditional-family.rationale: Said German women's chief duty lies in quiet work in the house and family; reported saying a nation is created by families, religion and traditions.

more-religion-public.rationale: Spoke of the necessity of faith, urged piety, daily Bible reading and prayers in the army, and said religion should be preserved for the nation.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Insisted on defending 'the great ideals' of art and tradition as a German duty and spoke of tradition in a monarchical state.

gradual-change.rationale: Memoirs: 'the road to compromise... has generally been my road'; his reforms (Easter 1917) were postponed to after the war.

revolution-justified.rationale: Memoirs treat the 1918 revolution as a betrayal and blame Social Democratic leaders; he declared Social Democrats enemies of the Empire.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Defended personal hereditary kingship throughout his reign: 'Kingship by God's grace' (Brandenburg 1899, Konigsberg 1910) and in the memoirs argued a monarch can and must shape the realm by personal participation.

democracy-best.rationale: Memoirs blame the 'parliamentary system' pressed on Germany by 'Utopians' and the revolution on Social Democrats; speeches present kingship by God's grace as the alternative to popular sovereignty.

political-violence-never.rationale: Ordered 'no quarter' in China, told recruits to shoot even kin if commanded, and wrote of drowning Socialists in a 'blood-bath'; he rejected the idea that political violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred: urged cultivating 'all warlike virtues' (Queen Louise speech) and called the army a school of manliness.

separate-church-state.rationale: As summus episcopus he worked for union of the Protestant churches and spoke of his rule as built on firm Christianity.

military-superiority.rationale: Wanted a fleet so strong that even the greatest sea power would risk its position by attacking it, and an army to make foes 'pause and think'; he denied seeking parity with Britain.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said the essence of nationality is demarcation by a boundary matching a nation's racial idiosyncrasies and blamed the old Reich for lacking a strictly national basis.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Memoirs: the Hohenzollern motto is 'to each his own', not, as Social Democrats would have it, 'to everyone the same'.

conscription.rationale: Memoirs praise general compulsory military service for its social and educational value, bringing rich and poor together.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Mixed: told Germans he wanted no new conquests, but pursued colonies, Kiaochow and a 'place in the sun' and spoke of overseas tasks for the new Empire.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Required recruits to swear personal loyalty to him ('one enemy, and that is my enemy') and spoke of the Hohenzollern monarchy as resting on the personal responsibility of the ruler.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said religion has never risen from science and is an overflowing of the heart, distinguishing revelation from scholarship (1903 letter and speech).

class-collaboration.rationale: Urged workers to cooperate with employers and the crown rather than follow Socialist class hatred; Easter 1917 spoke of unity between people and monarchy.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Held that great art and antiquity set eternal standards ('almost as good as 1900 years ago') and that artists must not abandon them; built and honoured museums.

workers-nation.rationale: Told Breslau workers to rely on king and fatherland and to send workers' representatives who were not Social Democrats; memoirs praise patriotic workers against internationalist leaders.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Said German women's duty lies in the home and family, not in meetings and 'imaginary rights'; did not address legislation directly.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Letters and interviews described Jews as an enemy 'Hebrew race' to be kept apart or punished, denying equal standing.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said the crown comes from God alone and 'not by parliament or by any assemblage of the people or by popular vote' (Konigsberg 1910).

population-transfer.rationale: In 1919-1922 remarks he wished Jews expelled from German soil and the press and endorsed pogroms; these were private or press remarks after abdication.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: 1897 speech said a party attacking the foundations of the state must be rooted out; yet memoirs describe compromise rather than open warfare on Social Democracy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: 1891 and 1906 remarks favoured force against the Socialists, but in 1890 he rejected Bismarck's plan for repression; evidence is mixed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Memoirs treat the monarch's personal command of army and navy and appointment of ministers as proper, and regret that in 1918 the government was deprived of command of the forces.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Memoirs condemn those who 'stabbed their own army in the back' in 1918 and Social Democrats who failed to prevent the revolution.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Defended Germany's alliance with Austria-Hungary and the Triple Alliance structure in the memoirs.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Memoirs: Alsace-Lorraine was ancient German soil and Germany could never voluntarily return it to France; yielding would have been a slap in the face.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Told students to keep to the whole field and not be disturbed by parties (Cassel 1911) and is quoted placing the king above party politics; he also urged national unity above party.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Described the imperial crown as a 'sacred jewel' held under God's protection and himself as answerable to Heaven, but claimed divine right rather than divine descent.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mixed: he said a king is responsible to God alone, yet the memoirs call himself a constitutional monarch bound to act with his chancellor.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Easter 1917 message affirms the enduring significance of the Prussian House of Lords while proposing only a broader membership; memoirs defend 'to each his own' and the monarchy's order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Told Cassel pupils to strive to know the history of their Fatherland and memoirs complain schools did not turn out youths conscious of being German.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hun speech charged troops to 'open the way to civilization', and at Saalburg praised Roman rule's civilizing effect on Germany.

patriotic-education.rationale: Memoirs: his school reform aimed at making pupils conscious Germans and regret that Germans were not educated to joy and pride in their fatherland; urged history of the Fatherland on students.

elective-rulers.rationale: Held that the crown is God-given and hereditary, explicitly not conferred by election or popular vote (Konigsberg 1910).

parliament-supreme.rationale: Memoirs lament that the parliamentary system was forced on the Empire in 1918 and that the government was deprived of command over army and navy; 1891 speech credited the army, not parliamentary majorities, with creating the Empire.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Accession vow to be a helper of the poor and oppressed; memoirs say the lord of the land must keep the welfare of the whole nation in mind.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Memoirs call French war aims to recover Alsace-Lorraine unjust and immoral.

military-guardian-role.rationale: 1891 speech told Guards recruits the army must be ready against enemies domestic and foreign, and that he trusted the army, not parliament, as the basis of the Empire.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Letters 1919-1927 and 1940 charged Jews with conspiring in revolution and world domination, memoirs report Great Orient Freemasons' role in preparing the war.

religion-illusion.rationale: Held religion to be real, God's revelation to mankind, not an illusion; 'No words of man have ever been uttered worthy of comparison with the words of Christ'.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Argued Alsace-Lorraine had been German soil for many centuries and was stolen by France.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mixed: called for rooting out the Socialist party (1897) and a bloodbath (1906 letter) but in 1890 refused Bismarck's plan to fight them with force and relied on compromise.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: At Konigsberg in 1910 he praised his grandfather for taking the crown as accorded by the will of God alone, not by parliament or popular vote, and spoke of himself as the chosen instrument of Heaven.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Strongly expanded and championed the army and navy; memoirs: 'keep your powder dry'.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Memoirs defend the Dual Alliance with Austria-Hungary and the policy of joining one bloc against the Entente.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Treated succession within the Hohenzollern line as natural and sacred; presented his son at Bonn as heir and spoke of his dynasty's God-given task.

property-franchise.rationale: Easter 1917 message states there is no room any longer for the Prussian three-class (wealth-weighted) franchise and promises direct, secret elections; memoirs say he wanted this as a gift to returning soldiers.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Accepted historical-critical findings in part (progressive revelation, Hammurabi's code) while holding to Luther's 'the Word'; mixed.

second-chamber.rationale: Easter 1917: praised the merits and lasting importance of the Prussian House of Lords and wanted it broadened.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mixed: repeatedly said forces serve only defence and peace (Strasburg 1908, memoirs) but sent a punitive expedition to China and spoke of a 'place in the sun'.

arms-reduction.rationale: Mixed: toasted the success of the 1899 Hague conference but reportedly scorned the Tsar's disarmament initiative, and expanded German arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Demanded unconditional obedience from soldiers, including shooting down relatives if ordered.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Mixed: 1903 letter says God revealed himself to heathens, Jews and Christians, yet treats Christ as the greatest revelation; later letters reject the Jewish God.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: dismissed women's pursuit of 'imaginary rights' to do as men do and political meetings.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: 1903 letter states the Old Testament contains many purely human-historical parts that are not God's revealed word and Sinai is only symbolically inspired, while holding Christ as the revealed Word.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Asked the people to help him not through the opposition of political parties but by confiding their difficulties to their sovereign, and criticized placing party above the whole.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Presented social legislation and loyalty to the Fatherland as going together for the working man (Breslau 1902, Easter 1917).

notes: Dead since 1941, so answers rest on his own speeches, letters, interviews and memoirs only; formal assent to Reichstag legislation is not counted. The antisemitic remarks date from exile (1919-1941) and are cited from Wikiquote's citations of Rohl; the 1922 Chicago Tribune and Bigelow 'gas' remarks were not used. Views on parliament and Social Democracy mix rhetoric of repression with policies of compromise (1890 refusal of Bismarck's plan; social legislation), so suppression answers are low. The Easter Message of 1917 was drafted with Bethmann Hollweg and is used only for the franchise and House of Lords.
